title: node-image-runtime-compatibility-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for validating node images, container runtimes, and GPU driver/CUDA/NCCL combinations for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Goal: provide a compact compatibility reference, terraform module notes for node pools, concrete upgrade/rollback steps, and repeatable validation checks for CI and on-site runs.

Scope:
- Kubernetes node image variants (ubuntu/rocky, kernel versions)
- Container runtimes (containerd, crio) and runtime config that impacts GPU drivers
- NVIDIA driver installation approaches (OS package, GPU-operator, driver-toolkit)
- CUDA and NCCL library versions used by models and inference runtime
- Terraform node pool lifecycle hooks and strategies for safe rolling updates
- Validation/SMOKE test commands and failure modes to detect

Executive summary (recommendations):
- Baseline supported stack for GA: Ubuntu 22.04 + kernel 5.15 (LTS) or 6.1 where validated, containerd >=1.6, NVIDIA driver 535.x + CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.17.2. This combo covers A100/H100 families with best perf and recent NCCL optimizations.
- GPU Operator is recommended for dynamic clusters; in locked enterprise air-gapped installs use the curated driver installer and pinned packages.
- For Terraform-managed node pools, prefer immutable node-image upgrades (new instance template + replace) over in-place driver swaps.

Compatibility matrix (text table - validated combos and notes):
- K8s 1.25 | Ubuntu 22.04 | kernel 5.15 | containerd 1.6 | driver 470.199 | CUDA 11.8 | NCCL 2.14 -> LEGACY: validated for V100; expect perf regressions on A100.
- K8s 1.26 | Ubuntu 22.04 | kernel 5.15 | containerd 1.6 | driver 535.113 | CUDA 12.1 | NCCL 2.17 -> RECOMMENDED: validated A100, H100 smoke & perf.
- K8s 1.26 | Rocky 9 | kernel 5.14 | containerd 1.7 | driver 535.113 | CUDA 12.1 | NCCL 2.17 -> PARTIAL: driver kernel modules required rebuild; test required for mlx devices.
- K8s 1.27 | Ubuntu 24.04-preview | kernel 6.1 | containerd 1.7 | driver 535.113/545.23 | CUDA 12.2 | NCCL 2.18 -> EXPERIMENTAL: validated only in lab with H100; some cc-minor flags for nv_peer_mem needed.
- Unsupported combinations: driver <450 with CUDA12.x, container runtime older than 1.5 with modern nvidia-container-toolkit.

Notes on variant-specific gotchas:
- Rocky/Alma kernels frequently ship older module build toolchains; pre-built driver binaries may not match. Always run dkms-mode validation step in CI.
- Containerd config: ensure "systemd_cgroup = true" when using nvidia-container-toolkit on modern runtimes to avoid OOM/kubelet cgroup misclassification.
- For CRI-O (crio), pin crio.conf log level and cgroup manager to systemd and validate seccomp profiles; otherwise GPU container startup can hang for ~20-60s.

Terraform module notes (node pool & lifecycle):
- Module recommendations: infra-modules/node-pool-v2 with following input knobs:
  - node_image (string): canonical image id rather than family name
  - gpu_driver_strategy (string): ["gpu-operator","host-installer","none"]
  - replace_on_image_change (bool): true by default for private-deploy
  - eviction_timeout_sec (number): defaults to 300
  - prebaked_drivers (bool): for airgap set true and point to local package repo
  - taints_on_upgrade (list): propagate to ensure critical pods are preserved
- Implementation notes: always create a new instance group/instance template and then migrate; do NOT attempt in-place apt-get/driver-install for production node pools.
- Example lifecycle: create new node template -> scale up new pool to 10% of capacity -> cordon/evict old nodes -> scale down old pool -> run post-check jobs against new pool.

Upgrade runbook (high level, meant for runbook automation and human ops):
1) Pre-checks (CI and cluster):
  - run: kubectl get nodes -o wide; verify Ready and gpu device allocatable >0
  - validate current drivers: kubectl run -i --rm --restart=Never driver-check --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-base -- nvidia-smi || gather node nsenter logs
  - validate scheduler: check PDBs and critical deployments (console, router, inference frontends)
2) Prepare new node image and validate in staging:
  - bake image with driver + containerd + runtime conf
  - run small perf suite: sample model latency 512 tokens, gbench, nccl-tests (all >90% of baseline)
3) Safe rolling update (automation preferred):
  - mark new instance group autoscaling limits and bring up small percentage (5-15%)
  - label new nodes with pool=new-image and run smoke pods that request GPUs
  - monitor kubelet logs and dmesg for NVML errors for 10-15 minutes after startup
  - progressively cordon/evict old nodes in waves, respecting PDBs
4) Post-checks:
  - run nccl-tests between GPUs on same and cross nodes
  - run perf regression harness comparing token throughput and tail latency
  - check kube-proxy/iptables/conntrack for any regressions
5) Rollback (if perf or stability failures):
  - scale new pool to zero or cordon and drain but keep running only if necessary
  - re-create old node template and scale back to previous capacity
  - escalate to platform on-call if driver kernel module oops appear

Validation scripts and commands (adoptable to CI runners):
- Node driver quick-check: kubectl debug node/<node> -it --image=ubuntu:22.04 -- bash -c "apt-get update && which nvidia-smi && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv"
- NV peer memory / RDMA check: run tests/rdma-health.sh (wrapper that runs ibv_rc_pingpong and checks dmesg for rdma errors)
- NCCL connectivity test (simplified): docker run --rm --gpus all nvcr.io/nvidia/nccl-tests:2.17.0 nccl-tests -b 8 -e 8M -f 2 -g 2 || collect logs /var/log/nccl-tests.log
- Kernel module build check: sudo dkms status; if modules not present run: sudo dkms autoinstall --verbose and re-check

Smoke test checklist (automated):
- Pod with nvidia.com/gpu allocation comes up within 45s.
- nvidia-smi returns driver name and version.
- A sample TF/PyTorch container runs a short inference and returns expected shape.
- NCCL tests complete without segmentation faults and show bandwidth within 80% of baseline.

Known flaky failures and mitigations:
- Symptom: Containers stuck at Init with message "could not select device plugin". Cause: nvidia-device-plugin v0.x incompatible with driver 535.x. Mitigation: pin device-plugin release aligned with driver version or use GPU operator.
- Symptom: nccl-tests OOM on small nodes. Cause: default per-process memory ballooning. Mitigation: cap CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and reduce batch sizes for validation.
- Symptom: Kernel oops after driver install on Rocky9. Cause: mismatched gcc/clang used to build modules. Mitigation: ensure build-essential and kernel-headers match exact kernel release, or use prebuilt vendor driver package.

Lab validation plan (short):
- Phase A: smoke matrix across 3 node images x 2 runtime configs x 2 driver strategies. Record pass/fail and time-to-ready.
- Phase B: perf regression with 3 model types (small LLM, medium encoder-decoder, embedding encode) using same input profile as production.
- Phase C: multi-node NCCL scaling with 2,4,8 GPUs (interop with RDMA)

Open action items / follow-ups:
- Add terraform variable to support prebaked kernel headers repository for airgapped installs (PD-4921).
- Bake reference AMIs for Ubuntu22.04-driver-535-cuda12.1 and publish image ids to confluence.
- Add a guardian CI job that runs quick-driver-check and nccl smoke on every node-image PR.

Appendix: quick references
- Helpful commands: kubectl describe node <node> | grep -i allocatable -A3; journalctl -u kubelet -f; dmesg | grep -i nvidia
- Helpful links: internal confluence PD-GPU-VALIDATION-2026; upstream nvidia-driver-release-notes; terraform module repo PR-312

Document history: notes and incremental checks are intentionally terse - this doc is a working playbook for teams building private deployment plans and will be iterated after each lab run.
